scientific.integrity: The proof reconstructs the published Ranger21 first step from Adaptive Gradient Clipping through Gradient Centralization, second-moment bias correction, and the Stable-Weight-Decay/Norm-Loss term. A strongly convex quadratic family makes the processed gradient exactly proportional to a mean-zero perturbation, yielding a closed inverse-distance singularity.
limitations: The claim is about the published Ranger21 Algorithm 4, not every later software implementation.
It requires positive regularization and a positive scheduled learning rate.
The example uses one parameter row and a deterministic strongly convex quadratic.
The exact singular point is accompanied by an unbounded neighborhood, but no empirical frequency claim is made.

title: Published Ranger21 has a gradient-centralization singularity in stable Norm Loss
